data.gender_notes: Devahansh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Devahansh is derived from the Sanskrit words ‘Deva’ (god) and ‘Hansh’ (treasure). The name signifies a god-given treasure or a divine blessing. In Hindu mythology, gods are believed to bestow their blessings upon their devotees, and the name Devahansh symbolizes this divine grace. The name Devahansh carries the meaning “God's Treasure” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Devahansh usually hope their child will grow to embody god's treasure and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Devahanshi was the name given to the Hindu goddess of fertility and abundance during the Shakta era. This period is believed to have occurred between the 6th and 13th centuries CE, primarily in parts of India including Bengal, Assam, and Karnataka.

The name 'Devahansh' is also mentioned in the Hindu epic 'Mahabharata', specifically in the 'Anushasana Parva', or 'Book of Instructions for Arjuna', where it is given as the name of a celestial nymph or 'Apsara' who is believed to reside in the heavenly abode of Indra.
